rows.claim: THE 50 is a burn program: leftover compute windows consumed by 50 tasks in 10 workstreams x 5, each task with a filed artifact as its finish line, so idle window decay converts into filed workdays.
rows.quote: Burn the remaining Flash windows and the Lite free window: 50 useful long-horizon
rows.steal: Any spare capacity is run as a fixed-shape wave program (N workstreams x M tasks) where the finish line is a filed artifact path, not a done message; open the program doc, fire by tier, close by artifact census.
rows.falsifier: A wave where task completion is claimed without an on-disk artifact path, or where more than a trivial fraction of finish-line paths resolve to nothing.

rows.claim: The launch law tiers dispatch: LANE items seed inbox rows, QUEUED items wait for a window, and OPERATOR items are the hard gates; nothing in the program requires a decision not already on file.
rows.quote: every LANE seeds a lane inbox row; every QUEUED waits for a window; OPERATOR items
rows.steal: Write the dispatch tier into the program doc itself ([LAUNCH NOW]/[LANE]/[QUEUED]/[OPERATOR]) so the run can be drained mechanically and the only human gates are pre-declared, not discovered mid-run.
rows.falsifier: A program task stuck waiting on an operator input that the launch doc did not mark OPERATOR, or a QUEUED item executed without a window.

rows.claim: The cwd bug lesson generalized: verifiers inherit the stray-path disease too; one that resolves finish-line claims relative to its own workspace cwd returned 0/44 on disk against 44/44 actually present, a 100% manufactured failure rate.
rows.quote: a verifier that resolves claims relative to its own cwd manufactures a 100% failure rate out of thin air
rows.steal: Verifier asks must carry absolute estate paths or recompute from the repo root before scoring; a verifier that cannot state its resolution root is disqualified from producing a pass/fail verdict.
rows.falsifier: A verifier run scoring 0 or 100 percent without a stated absolute-path resolution root, or a recount from absolute paths that disagrees with the verdict's 44/44.

rows.claim: When two verification passes disagree (builders all-ok vs verifier 0/44), the correct move is to audit the verifier itself before mourning the work; the correction here came from a second absolute-path recount, not from trusting either side.
rows.quote: Two verification passes disagreeing = check the checker before mourning the work.
rows.steal: On verifier-vs-builder disagreement, re-run verification under a different resolution scheme (absolute paths, byte sizes) before accepting either result; fold-by-script plus verify-by-disk beats both self-report and a single verifier.
rows.falsifier: A disagreement resolved by redoing the work instead of reproducing the verifier's failure, or a second recount that confirms the original 0/44.

rows.claim: The relaunch verdict scopes its claim to existence on disk and explicitly defers quality to a next wave; existence verdicts must not quietly impersonate quality verdicts.
rows.quote: this verdict claims EXISTENCE on disk, not quality
rows.steal: Split verification into two named passes (existence census, quality spot-review) and print the scope on the verdict itself so a 44/44 existence green cannot be cited later as a quality certification.
rows.falsifier: A verdict stating a coverage number without labeling its scope, or an existence pass whose output is later cited as quality assurance.
